messages:
maya: Heads-up — Parakeet int4 bringup is showing cluster degeneracy on the wiki holdout. Short-query recall@1 dropped from 0.74 -> 0.61 after quantization. Anyone seen this pattern before?

raj: Oof. Is that per-channel quant or symmetric/int4-tensor? Also what does recall@10 look like?

maya: Per-channel dynamic quant via our ONNX int4 pipeline. Recall@10 is mostly stable (0.89 -> 0.87). The failing set is short queries (titles, 3-6 tokens). HDBSCAN also made ~40% more singletons after quant.

olivia: Could be norm collapse or small-angle distortion. Do you normalize embeddings before indexing/search?

maya: Yes — we normalize both index and query vectors. I tried normalizing pre- and post-quant, no meaningful change.

dmitri: Can you drop the minimal repro and index params?

maya: Sure, quick snippet below (same one I used):

```python
# quick eval
import numpy as np
embs = model.embed(batch_queries)   # shape (N, D)
embs = embs / np.linalg.norm(embs, axis=1, keepdims=True)
index_embs = np.load('index_embs.npy')
index_embs = index_embs / np.linalg.norm(index_embs, axis=1, keepdims=True)
# simple dot product search
scores = embs @ index_embs.T
ranks = np.argmax(scores, axis=1)
```

HNSW params I used: `ef_construction=200`, `M=48`, `ef_search=128`. Index was built on quantized embeddings (int4 unpacked -> float via dequant table).

ci-bot: test-run: parakeet-int4-holdout-eval started (job 12233).

olivia: Two quick ideas: 1) try inner-product on raw (unnormalized) embeddings vs cosine — sometimes quant noise affects norm more than angle; 2) try asymmetric per-channel quant (scale + zero_point) rather than pure symmetric, reduces bias for low-dim features.

raj: Also compare to FP16 baseline on the same holdout to rule out calibration mismatch. What are FP16 numbers?

maya: FP16 run shows recall@1 = 0.75 on the short-query set (baseline float32 = 0.76). So FP16 is fine, issue only after int4.

dmitri: Another angle: check distribution of dot products before/after quant. If many near 1.0 get squashed non-linearly, that hurts top-1. Also HDBSCAN singletons rising suggests inter-point distances increased — could be anisotropic quant error.

maya: I pulled a quick delta plot: many high-confidence positives drop 0.05-0.12 in cosine score after quant.

olivia: If that's the case, a lightweight calibration step might help: learn a per-dimension scale vector alpha (small reg) on a tiny calibration set to restore top-k ordering. Quick pseudo:

```python
# calibration: find alpha to minimize rank loss (very small reg)
cal_embs = emb_calib / np.linalg.norm(emb_calib, axis=1, keepdims=True)
# optimize alpha s.t. (cal_embs * alpha) @ index_embs.T restores ranks
```

raj: Also try rebuilding index on float embeddings but search using dequantized queries (or vice-versa) to isolate whether index quantization or query quantization is the bigger offender.

maya: Good plan. I'll run: (A) index float / query dequant, (B) index dequant / query float, (C) asymmetric per-channel int4, (D) small calibration vector. Will post numbers.

indexer-bot: indexing job 12234 queued for scenario (A).

dmitri: If (A) fixes top-1 then we probably need to avoid quantizing the index for short-query workloads or selectively keep high-value shards in higher precision.

maya: Action items: I'll run the 4 variations, dump delta histograms and nearest-neighbor examples (good and broken cases). Olivia — can you try the calibration toy on a small shard? Raj — can you prepare a short query-only eval harness to run nightly if we see this pattern again?

olivia: On it, will try calibration + asymmetric quant later today.

raj: I'll put together the harness and add a regression alert if short-query recall@1 changes by >0.05 after quant.

maya: Thanks — will report back with numbers. :pray:
